operations.specification: Service layer will create a new user record upon successful validation of email uniqueness and password complexity rules. Passwords will be hashed before storage. The operation creates JWT tokens for authenticated sessions upon success. Database transaction handled to rollback on failure. Validation errors are returned for duplicate email or invalid inputs. Integration with email verification system possible but out of scope here.
operations.description: This API operation allows an unauthenticated user to register a new account by providing a unique email and password, fulfilling the join operation requirements for the user actor. operations.description: This API operation allows authenticated users to refresh their JWT tokens using a valid refresh token, fulfilling the token refresh operation requirements for the user actor. Security restrictions ensure users can only access user data they are authorized to view, protecting user privacy and data confidentiality.

This operation interacts with the multi_user_todo_users database table containing registered user accounts with email and password credentials, display names, and other user profile details.

The request body supports multiple search parameters and pagination controls using the IMultiUserTodoUser.IRequest type.

The response body returns a paginated list of user summary objects with essential properties for UI display, following the IPageIMultiUserTodoUser.ISummary type.

Typical use cases include user management interfaces and administrative consoles.

operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the multi_user_todo_users table applying filters from the request body such as email, display name, account status, and registration date range.
Implement pagination using page number and page size parameters.
Allow sorting by email, display name, or registration date.
Check authorization: allow only admin users or the user themself to access user data.
Return paginated results with total count and data array.
Handle errors for unauthorized access and invalid requests with appropriate HTTP status codes.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of user summary objects

operations.description:
Retrieve the profile information of the authenticated user.

This endpoint returns the user's account details, including their unique email address and display name. It is accessible only by authenticated users and enforces strict authorization to prevent access to other users' profiles.

The underlying database entity is multi_user_todo_users, which securely stores user credentials and profile data.

Because the user's identity is derived from the authentication context, there are no path parameters or request body.

Response includes all pertinent user profile fields except sensitive credentials like password hashes.

Expected errors include unauthorized access if the user is not authenticated.
operations.name: at

Query multi_user_todo_users table filtering by authenticated user's ID. Return sensitive fields omitted such as password hash. No path parameters or request body required. Return 401 Unauthorized if authentication fails. Use standard error handling middleware for other errors.

operations.description:
Update the authenticated user's profile with a new display name.

This API operation enables a logged-in user to modify their profile display name. The system enforces that users can only update their own profiles, ensuring privacy. The display name field is validated and updated in the underlying multi_user_todo_users database entity representing user accounts.

Security considerations include mandatory authentication, and access control prevents any user from modifying profiles other than their own.

Validation rules enforce that the display name meets acceptable formats before saving the changes.

This operation complements GET /users/profile (fetch own profile) and adheres to privacy-centric design principles.

Errors are returned for unauthorized access, validation failures, or system issues during update.
operations.name: updateProfile
operations.specification:
Perform authentication validation to ensure the user is logged in.
Load the user's current profile from users database table.
Validate the received display name for required format, length, and content.
Update the display name in the users table within a transaction.
Return the updated user profile entity.
Handle errors appropriately including validation and authorization errors.

responseBody.description: The updated user profile including the new display name.

requestBody.description: Updated profile data including new display name.

operations.description:
This API endpoint permanently deletes the authenticated user's account and all associated data, including todos and their edit histories.

According to the business requirements, when a user requests account deletion, the system must irreversibly delete the user's profile and all associated todos regardless of their state (active, soft deleted/trash) along with their entire edit history. This ensures complete privacy and data removal.

Security considerations include enforcing that only the authenticated user can initiate deletion of their own account, preventing unauthorized deletions.

The underlying database operations will perform cascading deletions that remove the user record and all dependent entities such as todos and todo edit histories.

This operation is critical for compliance with data privacy policies and user control over their data.

Clients should be aware that this action is irreversible and results in permanent loss of the user's data.

No request body or parameters are required, authentication context supplies the user identity.

Return HTTP 204 No Content on success.

Usecases related to this operation include user account management API suite with signup, login, and password change endpoints.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Implement user account deletion by authenticating the user token and identifying the user ID.

Perform database operations to permanently delete the user record.
Cascade delete all todos associated with the user.
Cascade delete all edit history entries linked to those todos.
Ensure database transactions handle integrity and rollback on failures.

Return status HTTP 204 No Content to indicate successful permanent deletion.

Validate that the user has no remaining dependencies before deletion.
Handle error cases such as user not found or authorization failure explicitly.

Log the deletion action for audit and security monitoring.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of user sessions with filtering and sorting options.

This operation allows authenticated users to query their own active and expired sessions. The response includes session metadata such as IP address, client URL, referrer, creation time, update time, expiration, and deletion status.

Authorization requires that users can only access session records associated with their user ID. The system enforces strict access control to maintain privacy.

Search options include filtering by expiration status, date ranges, and session activity. Sorting supports multiple sortable fields.

This endpoint typically works with user authentication APIs to facilitate session management and monitoring. Pagination parameters control the page size and number of results returned for efficient data handling.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query multi_user_todo_user_sessions table filtering by user ID to restrict access to own sessions. Support filters for session expiration, creation date ranges, and deletion status. Apply sorting on creation and expiration timestamps. Implement pagination with page and pageSize parameters. Return results as a paginated list of session summaries with total counts. Ensure authorization checks to prevent unauthorized access. Handle edge cases such as no matching sessions gracefully with empty lists. Integrate with user authentication subsystem for session lifecycle management.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of user session summaries

operations.description:
This endpoint allows secure updating of password reset information using a reset token. The token is verified against stored entries in multi_user_todo_user_password_resets, checking expiry and association with valid user accounts. Upon valid token verification, the password reset process proceeds, updating the user's password securely.

Security considerations restrict this operation to token holders, ensuring unauthorized access is prevented. Tokens are single-use and expire after a configured period, invalidating older requests.

The operation interacts with multi_user_todo_users implicitly by updating user credentials indirectly. It requires validation to ensure token uniqueness and expiration integrity.

Validation rules mandate presence of token and new password in request body. Errors are returned for expiration or invalid tokens.

This API complements authentication features and must be used as part of a secure password reset workflow.
operations.name: updatePasswordReset
operations.specification:
Validate the supplied reset token from the request body against multi_user_todo_user_password_resets records ensuring it exists and is not expired.

If valid, securely update the associated user's password with the new password provided.

Ensure transactional integrity and log the reset event.

Return appropriate success or error response depending on verification and update results.

This operation queries the multi_user_todo_user_password_resets table containing password reset tokens issued to users who requested password recovery. It returns fields such as the reset token, associated user ID, expiration datetime, and whether the token has been used.

Security constraints strictly limit access to authenticated users or authorized system roles to protect sensitive password reset information.

The endpoint takes a path parameter `id` which is the UUID of the password reset record. This ensures that token references are secure and unguessable.

This facilitates clients verifying password reset request status and supports further password recovery actions.

Typical error handling includes returning 404 if no record matches the requested ID, and 401 for unauthorized access attempts.

This operation is part of the Authentication and Password Management API suite, complementing endpoints for login, signup, and password change.

If record is found, return the entire entity including token, expiration, userId, and usage flag.

If not found, return a 404 error response.

If unauthorized, return a 401 error response.

It operates on the multi_user_todo_user_password_resets table, creating a new reset token record linked to the user email.

Security considerations include accepting requests without authentication but verifying the email exists before token creation.

No response body is returned as the operation triggers an asynchronous process.

Errors will be returned if the email format is invalid or if the system fails to process the request.

operations.description:
Verify user email ownership by processing a submitted verification token.

This endpoint accepts an encoded token typically sent via email after user registration. The token is validated against existing stored tokens in the multi_user_todo_user_email_verifications table.

Successful verification marks the user's email as confirmed and may enable further account activation steps.

Authorization and Security:
- Generally accessible without full authentication since users verifying email may not be fully logged in yet.
- Must validate token authenticity and expiry.

Database interaction:
- Look up token in multi_user_todo_user_email_verifications table.
- Confirm token is valid and not expired.
- Mark email as verified for associated user in multi_user_todo_users table.
- Handle invalid or expired tokens with appropriate errors.

Validation:
- Validate input token format.
- Ensure idempotent operations where repeated submissions of the same token do not cause errors.
- Return meaningful errors for expired or invalid tokens.

Related operations:
- POST /auth/signup to initiate user registration and trigger sending verification emails.

Expected behavior:
- On success, respond with verification confirmation.
- On failure, respond with descriptive validation error.
operations.name: processEmailVerification
operations.specification:
Implementation Details:
1. Receive a PATCH request with the verification token in the request body.
2. Query the multi_user_todo_user_email_verifications table for a matching token that is not expired.
3. If token is valid, update the corresponding user record in multi_user_todo_users to mark email as verified.
4. Remove or deactivate the used verification token to prevent reuse.
5. Return a success response with verification status.
6. If token is invalid or expired, return an error response indicating failure.
7. This operation does not require authenticated user context but must ensure security checks on token validity.
8. Handle concurrent requests idempotently to avoid race conditions.
9. Rely on database transactions to ensure atomicity.

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific email verification token by its unique ID.

This API operation allows authorized users to fetch the email verification token record associated with their account. It includes key properties such as the token string, expiration time, and verification status. This operation maps directly to the multi_user_todo_user_email_verifications database table.

Security is critical: only authorized users should access their own tokens. The service enforces ownership validation to prevent data leaks.

The response provides audit timestamps including creation, update, and deletion (soft delete) times, enabling client-side audit and compliance features.

This operation is commonly used during the email verification workflow to check token validity and status.

In case the token does not exist or requesting user is unauthorized, the operation should respond with appropriate HTTP error codes.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1. Validate the requesting user's authorization and ensure they own the email verification token identified by the UUID path parameter 'id'.
2. Query the multi_user_todo_user_email_verifications table by primary key 'id'. Include fields: id, multi_user_todo_user_id, token, expires_at, verified_at, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at.
3. If found and authorized, return the full email verification record in the response body.
4. If not found or unauthorized, return 404 or 403 HTTP status accordingly.
5. No request body is required as this is a simple GET operation.
6. Audit and logging should capture access events for security monitoring.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the email verification token
parameters.name: id

operations.description:
This endpoint creates a new email verification record linked to a specific user in the multi_user_todo system. It records the unique token, expiration date, and associates it with the user's ID. The record includes timestamps for creation and updates, and supports soft deletion through a deleted_at timestamp.

Security considerations restrict this operation to admin actors managing user email verifications. The verification token must be unique and securely generated.

The database entity multi_user_todo_user_email_verifications provides the storage structure for this data, with relationships ensuring user data consistency.

Validation ensures token uniqueness and correct timestamp formats. Related operations include GET endpoints to retrieve verification status or validate tokens, which should be implemented separately.

Errors may be returned for invalid user references, duplicate tokens, or expired tokens during subsequent verification attempts.
operations.name: createEmailVerification
operations.specification: Implement POST /email-verifications to insert a new record into multi_user_todo_user_email_verifications. Validate the multi_user_todo_user_id exists in multi_user_todo_users. Ensure token uniqueness with @@unique constraint. Set created_at and updated_at timestamps automatically. Handle soft delete with deleted_at. Return the full email verification record upon success. Authorize access to admin actors only.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of todos for the authenticated user.

This operation allows filtering todos by completion status (all, complete, incomplete) and sorting by creation date, start date, or due date in ascending or descending order.

Supports pagination to efficiently navigate large lists of todos. The response provides summarized todo information optimized for list displays.

Access is restricted to authenticated users; only their own todos are returned.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_todos table filtering by the authenticated user's ID.
Apply filters based on completion status: all, complete, or incomplete.
Support sorting by creationDate, startDate, or dueDate with asc or desc order.
Apply pagination parameters page and pageSize.
Return paginated results with total count and current page info.
Use database indexes on userId and completion status for performance.
Validate request body for correct filter and paging values.
Return results as IMultiUserTodoTodo.ISummary DTO array wrapped in IPageIMultiUserTodoTodo.

operations.description:
Retrieve full details of a single todo item by its unique identifier.

This endpoint returns the complete information of the todo including title, description, start date, due date, completion status, and creation date, as specified in the multi_user_todo_todos database schema. 

Access is restricted to authenticated users, and users can only retrieve their own todos. Authorization checks are mandatory to ensure data privacy.

This operation is related to other todo management endpoints like POST /todos for creation, PATCH /todos/{todoId} for updates, and GET /todos for listing todos.

The API does not accept a request body, as all necessary identification is done via path parameter.

Proper error handling should be included for cases such as todo not found or unauthorized access.

Fetch the todo from multi_user_todo_todos table using provided todoId. Verify the todo belongs to the authenticated user. If not found or unauthorized, return appropriate error.

Return comprehensive todo information including title, description, start date, due date, completion status, and creation date.
Validation of todoId as UUID format is required.
No additional query parameters are needed.

operations.description:
Create a new todo item for the authenticated user.

This endpoint accepts a JSON payload containing the todo title (required), an optional description, and optional start and due dates. Upon successful creation, the todo is stored with a default incomplete status and associated with the user who created it.

Security considerations ensure that only authenticated users can create todos, and each todo is uniquely linked to its creator to protect data privacy.

The response returns the complete information of the created todo, including its unique identifier, timestamps, and current status.

Associated operations include:
- PATCH /todos/{id} for updating todo details
- GET /todos for retrieving the user's todo list
- DELETE /todos/{id} for deleting a todo (soft delete)

Error handling returns appropriate HTTP status codes for validation errors, authentication failures, and other edge cases.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Perform validation to ensure the 'title' field in the request body is non-empty.
Associate the newly created todo entry with the authenticated user ID.
Set default completion status to false (incomplete).
Insert the new todo into the multi_user_todo_todos table.
Return the full todo item details as the response.
Handle errors for validation failures and user authentication.
Ensure operation is transactional to maintain data integrity.

requestBody.description: New todo creation data including title, optional description, start date, and due date.

operations.description:
Update an existing todo by its unique identifier.

This operation permits a user to modify the title, description, start date, and due date of their todo. The completion status and soft delete status are not modifiable through this endpoint.

Security is enforced so that users can update only their own todos. Unauthorized edits are prevented.

The operation directly modifies the `multi_user_todo_todos` table, updating relevant fields.

Validation rules from business requirements are applied, such as non-empty title.

If the todo does not exist or does not belong to the requesting user, an appropriate error is returned.

Clients should use the GET /todos/{todoId} endpoint to fetch the updated todo details after an update.

Error responses include validation errors and authorization failures.

Related operations:
- POST /todos to create new todos
- PATCH /todos/{todoId}/toggle to toggle completion status
- DELETE /todos/{todoId} to soft delete todos
- GET /todos/{todoId} to fetch todo details
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Perform validation of input fields ensuring title is non-empty and conforms to rules.
Verify that the todo with given todoId exists and belongs to the authenticated user.
Update the multi_user_todo_todos table fields: title, description, startDate, dueDate.
Do not modify completion status or deleted flag here.
Handle transactions to ensure data integrity.
Return the updated todo entity as response.
Handle errors for validation, authorization, and not found cases.

operations.description:
This API operation permanently deletes a todo item by its unique identifier (todoId). The deletion removes the todo record entirely from the database, including all associated edit history entries as required by the business rules. This endpoint is used by authenticated users to manage their todos securely.

Security-wise, only the owner of the todo can perform this deletion. Authorization checks ensure that a user cannot delete todos belonging to others.

This operation relates closely to the trash management API, where deleted todos can also be permanently removed from the system. It completes the lifecycle of a todo by allowing irreversible removal.

In case of errors, appropriate HTTP status codes and messages will be returned, such as 404 if the todo does not exist or 403 if attempting unauthorized delete.

No request body is necessary. The todoId is provided as a path parameter in UUID format.

Response body is empty, indicating successful completion without returning data.

Attempt to delete the todo record from multi_user_todo_todos table.
Cascade deletion or transactional removal of all associated edit history entries from multi_user_todo_todo_edit_histories table.
Handle cases where todoId not found by returning a 404 error.
Return 204 No Content on successful deletion.
Ensure database transactions enforce consistency.
Log deletion actions for audit trail.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of edit history entries associated with a specific todo item.

This operation allows an authenticated user to query the edit history records of their todo, facilitating review of past changes such as title, description, start date, and due date modifications. The results are paginated and sorted by most recent change by default.

Security ensures that only the owning user can access the history entries of their own todo items, maintaining privacy and data integrity.

The underlying data model corresponds to the multi_user_todo_todo_edit_histories table, which tracks each edit with timestamps and changed fields. This API provides a summary view optimized for historical browsing.

Clients should use this API to implement UI components showing change logs and audit trails for todos.

Typical use includes filtering by date range, pagination page size, and sorting order as supported in the IRequest schema.

This API complements the todo management endpoints to provide a comprehensive todo lifecycle history.

Errors such as unauthorized access or invalid todoId will return appropriate HTTP status codes with error messages.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement pagination and sorting based on request body criteria.
Validate todoId path parameter format as UUID.
Query multi_user_todo_todo_edit_histories filtering by todoId.
Ensure user authorization for ownership of the todo.
Sort records by edit timestamp descending by default.
Return data as paginated summary objects.
Handle error cases for invalid ids, unauthorized access, and empty results gracefully.

This API is part of the Todo Management feature set, enabling users to track and review the chronological record of changes made to their tasks.

Security considerations ensure that unauthorized access is denied, and proper validation is performed on identifiers.

Related operations include listing all edit histories for a todo (GET /todos/{todoId}/editHistories) and restoring from trash operations.

Return the full edit history record including fields: id, todo_id, edit_timestamp, changed_title, changed_description, changed_start_date, changed_due_date.

Raise 404 if not found or unauthorized.

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page. Actual count may be less on last page.

records.description:
Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not
just the current page. This value is computed via a COUNT query and is
essential for calculating total pages and displaying pagination UI
elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".
records.x-autobe-specification: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available.

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When
records is 0, pages will also be 0. This value enables clients to render
page navigation controls and validate page bounds.

statistics.

This interface provides comprehensive pagination information returned
alongside paginated list data. It enables clients to implement navigation
controls, display progress indicators, and determine data boundaries for UI
rendering.

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.
